originalTitle: September surge or October offload? Jobs experts weigh in on this fall’s hiring trends
summary: The "September surge" might boost hiring this fall, but the Fed rate hike could slow down the job market. Here's what experts say to do.
content:
Job seekers and career experts alike are hoping that fall will bring an uptick in the job market, popularly known as the "September surge."

It's natural for hiring to ramp up at the beginning of autumn, says career coach Colleen Paulson: People are "back in the groove" after their vacations and coasting off back-to-school energy.

"No matter what the market is, I think we'll always see that pick-up," she says.

The job market has been looking more positive in recent months: After a slow summer , the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August , marking this year's highest increase since March.

"We want to be optimistic," Paulson says. "There are so many people out there that have been looking for a long time , and they're looking for some hope."

Here's what Paulson and other experts say about this fall's job market trends, from hiring "bumps" to Fed rate-related slowdowns.

What will the 'September surge' look like this year?

Amanda Augustine, a career coach and resume writer, says she expects to see a "bump" in hiring this fall, rather than a "surge."

But it's unlikely that momentum will last through the rest of the fall, according to Augustine, and "while it's a bit more of a positive job market, that doesn't mean it's necessarily going to be an easy job market for everyone."

Many companies are only hiring new employees to solve specific business needs, Augustine says: they're looking for a candidate who possesses "the missing skill that's required in order to complete this project, meet this target, build this business solution."

"We are seeing pockets of hiring, but it's not an even distribution across the board," she says.

The Fed rate change could also affect hiring

On Sept. 16, the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate to a range of 3.75% to 4%, its first increase since July 2023, in an effort to combat inflation .

Due to higher borrowing costs, businesses may become "more cautious" about hiring and other expansion plans, according to Annette Garsteck, a career coach based in Cleveland, Ohio.

It could also cause employers to suspend or delay hiring for positions they currently have open, she says.

"Maybe it just delays it right into October, November, December or they say, 'We're on a hiring freeze, and we'll revisit this position again next year.'"

Midterm elections are also coming up, Augustine says, which could cause employers to "pause and not necessarily take as many risks in hiring" until they can gauge how election results will affect the overall economy.

Is there going to be an 'October offload' like last year?

Last October, companies announced 153,074 job cuts , the highest number of cuts for that month since 2003 and a 183% surge from September 2025.

Despite better labor market conditions this year, Paulson says that many workers are still worried about potential layoffs in the fall.

"There's a lot of fear out there," Paulson says. "People have seen it in years past, and they know what could be potentially coming."

Since employers have been cautious about hiring this year, Augustine says it's unlikely that this October will be another "bloodbath."

Still, "companies are under this pressure to continue to cut costs and deliver more profit," which could motivate some employers to target benefits like parental leave and healthcare, Paulson says.

"Even if companies aren't laying [workers] off, they're kind of making it miserable for people to stick around," she says.

Both job seekers and employed workers need to be prepared for any scenario, Paulson says.

If you're on the job market right now, Paulson recommends setting up alerts on job boards and applying to new roles within 24 hours.

"You want to be a first mover here if you can," she says.

For workers who are worried about layoffs, Paulson advises them to update their resumes and make sure that they have access to any records they might need to illustrate their skills .

"Sometimes people will lose their jobs and then they lose access to all of those files," she says, so Paulson recommends preserving copies of your notable accomplishments and performance reviews .

Given the volume of applications that hirers receive, Garsteck recommends leveraging your relationships to get an introduction to somebody in the company: "Does your friend or your ex-work bestie know somebody at that organization? Can they introduce you? And can that person be the referral?"

Since many companies are leaning toward skills-based hiring right now, Augustine advises job seekers to "take a step back and inventory their skill set and compare it to what the market is valuing at the moment."

Then, you can build your job search strategy around "advertising or promoting what you have to offer and where it fits into the greater job landscape today."

chineseTitle: 九月激增还是十月抛售？就业专家对今年秋季的招聘趋势发表了看法
chineseSummary: “九月激增”可能会提振今年秋季的招聘，但美联储加息可能会放缓就业市场。这是专家所说的要做的事情。
chineseContent:
求职者和职业专家都希望秋季能够带来就业市场的回升，即俗称的“九月激增”。

职业教练科琳·保尔森 (Colleen Paulson) 表示，秋季初招聘人数增加是很自然的事情：人们在假期结束后“回到了最佳状态”，享受了返校的活力。

“无论市场如何，我认为我们总会看到这种回升，”她说。

近几个月来，就业市场看起来更加乐观：经历了一个缓慢的夏季之后，美国劳工统计局报告称，8 月份非农就业人数增加了 162,000 人，创下今年 3 月份以来的最高增幅。

“我们希望保持乐观，”保尔森说。 “有很多人已经寻找了很长时间，他们正在寻找希望。”

以下是保尔森和其他专家对今年秋季就业市场趋势的看法，从招聘“激增”到与美联储利率相关的放缓。

今年的“九月高峰”会是什么样子？

职业教练兼简历撰写者阿曼达·奥古斯丁表示，她预计今年秋季的招聘会出现“激增”，而不是“激增”。

但奥古斯丁表示，这种势头不太可能持续到秋季剩余时间，“虽然就业市场更加积极，但这并不意味着对每个人来说都一定是一个轻松的就业市场。”

奥古斯丁说，许多公司只是雇佣新员工来解决特定的业务需求：他们正在寻找一位拥有“完成这个项目、实现这个目标、构建这个业务解决方案所需的缺失技能”的候选人。

“我们看到了一些招聘，但分布并不均匀，”她说。

美联储利率变化也可能影响招聘

9月16日，美联储将基准利率上调至3.75%至4%，这是自2023年7月以来的首次加息，以对抗通胀。

俄亥俄州克利夫兰的职业教练安妮特·加斯特克表示，由于借贷成本上升，企业可能会对招聘和其他扩张计划变得“更加谨慎”。

她说，这还可能导致雇主暂停或推迟招聘他们目前空缺的职位。

“也许只是将其推迟到十月、十一月、十二月，或者他们说，‘我们正在冻结招聘，明年我们将再次重新考虑这个职位。’”

奥古斯丁表示，中期选举也即将到来，这可能会导致雇主“暂停，不一定会在招聘方面承担那么多风险”，直到他们能够评估选举结果将如何影响整体经济。

Is there going to be an 'October offload' like last year?

Last October, companies announced 153,074 job cuts , the highest number of cuts for that month since 2003 and a 183% surge from September 2025.

保尔森表示，尽管今年劳动力市场状况有所改善，但许多工人仍然担心秋季可能出现的裁员。

“那里有很多恐惧，”保尔森说。 “人们在过去的几年里已经看到了这一点，他们知道可能会发生什么。”

Since employers have been cautious about hiring this year, Augustine says it's unlikely that this October will be another "bloodbath."

保尔森表示，尽管如此，“公司仍面临着继续削减成本和提供更多利润的压力”，这可能会促使一些雇主瞄准产假和医疗保健等福利。

“即使公司不裁员，他们也会让留下来的人感到痛苦，”她说。

保尔森说，求职者和就业工人都需要为任何情况做好准备。

如果您现在正在求职市场上，保尔森建议您在求职板上设置提醒并在 24 小时内申请新职位。

“如果可以的话，你想成为这里的先行者，”她说。

对于担心裁员的工人，保尔森建议他们更新简历，并确保他们能够获得任何可能需要的记录来证明自己的技能。

“有时人们会失去工作，然后他们就无法访问所有这些文件，”她说，因此保尔森建议保留您的显着成就和绩效评估的副本。

考虑到招聘者收到的申请数量，加斯特克建议利用你的关系来介绍公司中的某个人：“你的朋友或前工作好友认识该组织中的某个人吗？他们可以介绍你吗？那个人可以作为推荐人吗？”

由于许多公司目前倾向于基于技能的招聘，奥古斯丁建议求职者“退后一步，盘点他们的技能，并将其与目前市场的估值进行比较。”

然后，您可以围绕“广告或宣传您所提供的产品以及它适合当今更大的工作环境”来制定您的求职策略。
